title: Inquest called into death of Niagara Detention Centre inmate
article: A corner's inquest has been called into the winter 2011 death of a prisoner at the Niagara Detention Centre.
Randall Fawcett, 25, of Niagara Falls, died on Dec. 29, 2011 while in custody.
Inquests are mandatory under the Coroners Act when someone dies a non-natural death in prison.
Regional supervising coroner Dr. Jack Stanborough said it's expected evidence will be heard that Fawcett's death was toxicological.

"We'll be exploring the circumstances of his death and making any recommendations around that," said Stanborough, adding it's not a unique scenario but there may be opportunity for the jury to make recommendations for preventing similar deaths.
The coroner's office has two other Niagara cases it plans to probe with a jury in the future.

Stanborough said an inquest will be called into the death of 18-year-old Ryan Dube, who fell over a Niagara gorge retaining wall to his death on July 24, 2012 while pursued by a police officer in Niagara Falls. The Special Investigations Unit cleared Niagara Regional Police Const. Jacob Smits of any wrongdoing in August.
The death of 46-year-old Kelvin Sawa, who died from injuries suffered at the Niagara Detention Centre on Aug. 15, 2011, will also be the subject of an inquest but it will be years down the road.
Two men who shared a prison ward with Sawa are charged with second-degree murder in that case. The inquest won't be held until the criminal matters wrap up.
Fawcett's inquest is being held June 3 at 9:30 a.m. at the Welland Courthouse. It's expected to last three days and hear from approximately seven witnesses.
